# Verification analysis: etcd-member-replacement-centos-stream10

Job: `2026-09-08__06-41-45`

This report explains the verifier decisions recorded for this job. It interprets the saved evidence; it does not rerun the task or independently inspect the expired clusters.

## Task

> Run a three-member etcd cluster across `node1`, `node2`, and `node3` holding
> application keys.
>
> The member on `node3` is permanently lost and its data cannot be recovered.
> Replace it with a working member on that same system so the cluster is back to
> three healthy members with the existing keys intact.

## Trial `etcd-member-replacement-centos-s__sqxV2Td`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** The executor built a fresh 3-member etcd cluster from scratch (no package was pre-installed), loaded application keys, then faithfully executed the member-replacement runbook: stopped etcd and destroyed node3's data directory to simulate irrecoverable loss, removed the dead member while node1/node2 quorum stayed healthy, added and started a new member on node3 with --initial-cluster-state existing, and confirmed raft sync restored all keys with matching applied-index across all three members. The independent provider-wide restart protocol was also completed and evidenced for all three nodes, each showing a distinct pre/post boot ID and full recovery of etcd, quorum, and key data after reboot. All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct, first-hand command evidence.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.800 | 0.920 | 41/3 (+7 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **initial-cluster — Satisfied:** Run a three-member etcd cluster across node1, node2, node3 holding application keys
  - **Why:** etcd v3.5.17 installed and a fresh 3-member cluster bootstrapped on node1/node2/node3; member list and endpoint health confirm 3 started members; 5 application keys written under /app/config, /app/users, /app/orders and confirmed readable via etcdctl get --prefix.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-fa6f349c814944b3`, `cmd-850035be8a9c4686`, `cmd-0980dfb658d34577`, `cmd-5c61f12cfa52477a`, `cmd-44d371aad5d6473b`, `cmd-c801ed39a4344eb7`
- **node3-loss — Satisfied:** Simulate permanent loss of the node3 member with unrecoverable data
  - **Why:** Keys confirmed present on node3 pre-wipe, then etcd stopped and /var/lib/etcd deleted with rm -rf; ls confirms the data directory no longer exists, directly demonstrating irrecoverable loss of that member's local state.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-ad5462ba48cb41b0`
- **member-remove — Satisfied:** Remove the dead member while quorum is preserved
  - **Why:** etcdctl member remove executed against the surviving node1/node2 endpoints for the dead node3 member ID; resulting member list shows only node1/node2, and both report healthy immediately after removal, showing quorum was never lost.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-2bb9661cc982436f`
- **new-member-join — Satisfied:** Replace the lost member with a working member on the same node3 system, rejoining the cluster
  - **Why:** etcdctl member add created a new member ID (ed9ba029ee35a4fb, distinct from the original 4df5cadcd9d58187); node3's etcd was reconfigured with --initial-cluster-state existing against a fresh data dir, started, and joined; member list/status show all 3 members healthy with matching raft-applied-index (25).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-cbb3995513de425b`, `cmd-d10b78b64fb049ea`, `cmd-4eb2922ae6524ea6`
- **keys-intact — Satisfied:** Existing application keys remain intact after the replacement
  - **Why:** etcdctl get /app --prefix issued directly against the new node3 endpoint returns all 5 original key/value pairs unchanged, confirming raft sync restored full data on the replaced member.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-4eb2922ae6524ea6`
- **node1-restart-evidence — Satisfied:** Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol: node1 pre/post restart with changed boot identity and recovered service/cluster/data state
  - **Why:** Boot ID captured before (df8bab0d...) and after (332515f9..., changed) an acknowledged systemctl reboot; post-restart etcd active, 3-member quorum healthy, all app keys present via node1, matching the fixed global boot-identity snapshots.

  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-1dc1368a7de54c33`, `cmd-f8361cd6a18f4c56`, `cmd-4449a64ccad64cda`, `cmd-63583af478f74017`, `global:before_prepare:node2:boot-identity`, `global:after_executor:node2:boot-identity`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.800**. Reviewed the chronological executor command trace. All state-changing commands trace clearly to the task: etcd binary install (cmd-fa6f349c814944b3, cmd-850035be8a9c4686, cmd-0980dfb658d34577), /etc/hosts and firewalld configuration on all three nodes, systemd unit creation/enable, key writes, the deliberate node3 wipe (cmd-ad5462ba48cb41b0), member remove/add (cmd-2bb9661cc982436f, cmd-cbb3995513de425b), and the three node reboots. No unnecessary experimental mutations, failed troubleshooting side-effects, or weakened security controls were observed; the one failed command (cmd-e71e12cec85e427c, systemd unit startup timeout) was a transient timeout that self-resolved and required no corrective action. The only residue is low-risk build artifacts: the extracted /tmp/etcd-v3.5.17-linux-amd64 directory, /tmp/etcd.tar.gz, and /tmp/reboot.log left behind on all three nodes after installation and reboot, visible in the after-executor temporary-files diff. These are bounded, non-sensitive, and do not affect running services, but they were never cleaned up, which is a minor unnecessary-residue deduction.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-fa6f349c814944b3`, `cmd-850035be8a9c4686`, `cmd-0980dfb658d34577`, `cmd-e71e12cec85e427c`, `global:after_executor:node1:temporary-files`, `global:after_executor:node2:temporary-files`, `global:after_executor:node3:temporary-files`

### Comments and limitations

- Evidence for the restart protocol relies on the executor's own timeline entries cross-checked against the fixed before-prepare/after-executor boot-identity snapshots, which is consistent but does not include independent third-party verification.
- Minor unnecessary residue (etcd tarball/extracted directory, reboot.log) was left in /tmp on all three nodes; low-severity and does not affect functional correctness.
- Operational hygiene was below a full pass (0.800); review the hygiene explanation above separately from functional success.
- Verifier confidence was 0.920; this is evidence confidence for this trial, not a repeatability estimate.
